soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed d=0 reduction fails: 2^{J_n^* d}≈n^{2d/(4s+d)} becomes 1≈1 and leaves J_n^* wholly unspecified, while the tensor wavelet space still has growing outcome resolution; consequently neither the stated estimator tuning nor the Theorem 2 resolution condition reduces to the unconditional benchmark.

source_verification_receipts.locator: §3.3, Theorem 3.2 and the following Remark P=Q
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives a root-n CLT under 2s>d_Y+d_Z and states that conditional equality makes the squared COT estimator converge faster than n^{-1/2}.
For each fixed positive entropic regularization parameter, the null second-order estimator has an n-rate weighted centered chi-square limit.
The article studies distributional limits for squared empirical quantile processes integrated against weights, including weighted Wasserstein goodness-of-fit statistics.
The paper proves sharp rates for empirical optimal-transport costs with smooth costs, including easier estimation away from equality and matching lower bounds.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the single resolution rule by an outcome/covariate-resolved construction, or explicitly use total dimension d+1, and rederive every rate and stochastic restriction so the d=0 case selects a genuine outcome resolution and recovers the del Barrio benchmark.
State a fully normalized definition of the projected Hessian and local coordinates eta_{k,n}, including their n-scaling and the covariance whitening, before asserting the mixed-law approximation.

Replace the fixed function b in the lower-bound sentence with an explicit n-indexed sign-paired high-frequency family that preserves positivity, Hölder radius, shared marginal, and the required product-mixture divergence bound.

recommended_next_step: Pivot to a dimensionally coherent scalar-outcome projection and rederive the phase diagram before resubmitting this novelty angle.
